assessments.reasoning: OSI CMS record 466 matches the claimed representation digest. Its title names version 1.0 and its opening requires “Licensed under the Open Software License version 1.0” immediately following the work’s copyright notice.

The Index’s SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 admits historical editions and defines a license by a controlling source, identifiable text, edition and grant. OSI’s 1.0 publication satisfies that criterion.

OSI’s September 8, 2021 archive preserves Rosen’s request to remove pre-3.0 AFL and OSL versions and his endorsement of the 3.0 forms. McCoy Smith proposed retaining the earlier versions as superseded for legacy uses.

challenge.method: Compared the body notice with the 1.1 notice and tested Rosen’s phrase “no longer valid” against the 1.0 termination terms, approval metadata and SPDX deprecation field.
challenge.results: The notice specifies 1.0. Sections 8–9 identify conduct that triggers termination. The correspondence establishes no such conduct for any work. OSI’s approved=false, SPDX’s isOsiApproved=true and Rosen’s general recollection leave historical board action unresolved. SPDX records isDeprecatedLicenseId=false.

limitations: Historical describes the local reference. A particular grant, its termination, installation eligibility and a historical OSI board decision each require separate evidence.
reasoning: OSI publishes an identifiable 1.0 license with copyright, patent and source-code provisions. Its superseded category and Rosen’s treatment of pre-3.0 forms support the Index’s historical classification.
